Field surveys across several watersheds in western Tennessee and Kentucky have consistently recorded this size at maturity, with little variation among geographically distinct populations, suggesting a stable ontogenetic schedule under typical environmental conditions. The combination of rapid hatching at warm temperatures and a small birth mass suggests a strategy that prioritizes early emergence over the production of larger, more energetically fortified offspring.
